jobs.title: Regional Innovation Director, Productivity (BC)
jobs.description:
Regional Innovation Director, Productivity (BC)

Remote: BC

Salary: 120,000.00- $140,000.00

Opportunity Overview

At the Canadian Food Innovation Network (CFIN), we are committed to building Canada's most dynamic food innovation community. We bring together food businesses, innovators, researchers, industry partners and resources to help Canadian companies innovate, grow and compete.
CFIN is looking for a highly experienced Regional Innovation Director to bring hands-on manufacturing expertise and relationship-driven regional engagement to the BC food and beverage sector.
This is a dual-mandate role. As a Regional Innovation Director
, you will build and maintain a strong, visible presence for CFIN across BC, developing relationships throughout the food and beverage ecosystem, identifying opportunities for engagement and connecting companies with CFIN’s funding opportunities, innovation resources and national network. While your portfolio will span the broader food and beverage landscape, you will bring particular depth in food manufacturing and technology adoption. As a Certified SIRI Assessor
, you will deliver structured, on-site Smart Industry Readiness Index (SIRI) assessments for food and beverage processors, providing a clear, benchmarked view of their technology and manufacturing readiness. These assessments will also strengthen CFIN's ability to identify productivity opportunities and support informed technology adoption across the sector.
This role is best suited to someone who understands the practical realities of the plant floor and is equally comfortable building trusted relationships across the food sector and conducting rigorous, structured technology assessments. You will bring manufacturing credibility to conversations with processors while serving as a broader regional resource for food businesses looking for technologies, connections, funding opportunities and ways to advance their innovation goals.

About the Canadian Food Innovation Network

The Canadian Food Innovation Network (CFIN) is a national, member-based not-for-profit organization dedicated to advancing Canada's food business ecosystem. CFIN connects Canadian food businesses and their ecosystem partners with insights, ideas, technologies, programs and resources that strengthen business performance through innovation.
Joining CFIN means becoming part of a high-performing team that connects industry leaders, researchers and innovators to solve pressing challenges, advance transformative ideas and create practical solutions that enhance competitiveness and productivity in Canada's food sector.

What Makes CFIN Stand Out?

Collaborative Ecosystem: We build partnerships that bring diverse collaborators together and turn innovative ideas into meaningful outcomes.
Focus on Impact: CFIN supports commercialization projects that advance food science, technology and sustainability while addressing real industry challenges.
Industry-Led Initiatives: Guided by our members, Innovation Advisory Council and Board of Directors, we design funding programs, tools, workshops and resources that help innovators overcome barriers.

What you'll be doing:

Regional Engagement and Innovation Support

· Promote CFIN’s programs, services, membership benefits, events and other initiatives, helping companies and ecosystem partners understand how they can engage with CFIN.
· Build and maintain productive relationships with prospective and existing CFIN members, industry associations, innovation organizations and other regional stakeholders across BC’s broader food and beverage ecosystem. Develop a strong understanding of their business, operational and innovation needs and connect them with the people, resources and programs that can support their goals.
· Manage an active portfolio of high-touch BC members, proactively tracking their needs, interactions with CFIN, the support provided and outcomes achieved.
· Proactively identify opportunities for deeper member engagement, qualify leads based on need and potential value for additional CFIN services and move opportunities through the pipeline.
· Maintain a strong and credible in-market presence for CFIN through regular in-person and virtual engagement, company visits, industry events and speaking opportunities. Extend this presence into online spaces including LinkedIn and YODL to further engage members and champion their needs and accomplishments to a wider audience.

Manufacturing Technology Assessment (SIRI)

· Obtain and maintain Certified SIRI Assessor (CSA) certification through the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT) and use it to deliver Official SIRI Assessments for food and beverage manufacturers. All training and certification costs covered by CFIN.
· Conduct structured assessments of manufacturing facilities using the SIRI methodology, frameworks and tools to evaluate technology and manufacturing readiness, identify priority areas for improvement and provide a formal report of findings and recommendations.
· Translate insights from SIRI assessments into opportunities for CFIN to create additional value for members, informing the development of services and supports that address productivity needs and help strengthen and accelerate Canada’s domestic food processing sector.
· Capture and track assessment outcomes and insights to help demonstrate the value of SIRI assessments and inform CFIN's understanding of technology adoption and productivity opportunities across the sector.

Industry Intelligence & Collaboration

· Bring first-hand knowledge of the BC food and beverage manufacturing sector into CFIN’s planning and programming, identifying regional trends, emerging opportunities, industry challenges and evolving technology and innovation needs.
· Share insights and practical manufacturing knowledge with the broader RID team, helping colleagues strengthen their technical understand of food processing operations and the technologies being adopted across the sector.
· Identify and surface member insights, success stories and case study opportunities for consideration by CFIN’s Programs and Communications teams, helping demonstrate member and sector impact.
· Use data and performance metrics to track regional activity and outcomes, contribute to the development of meaningful KPIs that help CFIN measure progress towards departmental and organizational goals.
· Maintain accurate and timely records of stakeholder interactions, leads, referrals, opportunities and follow-up activities. Strong CRM discipline is essential to the role.
· Contribute manufacturing and regional perspectives to national planning, initiatives and cross-functional projects.

Travel and Regional Representation

· Travel within Western Canada for SIRI assessment work and within BC for meetings and industry events, representing CFIN professionally and consistently with its mission and values.
· Participate in occasional travel outside BC for national meetings, events or organizational priorities.

What you bring:

Education and Experience

· Bachelor’s degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) discipline is preferred.
· Significant hands-on experience in food or beverage manufacturing and production operations, with direct experience in automation, productivity improvement and capital investment decisions.
· Relevant consulting, advisory or technology-consulting experience is an asset and will support eligibility for SIRI Assessor certification.

Certification Requirement

· This role requires the successful candidate to obtain and maintain Certified SIRI Assessor (CSA) certification from the International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT) within the first 6 months of employment. This includes completing 40 hours of approved SIRI Assessor coursework and passing both the theory and practical CSA examinations.
· Successful completion of the CSA Examination is a condition of continued employment in this role.
· Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate that they meet at least one of INCIT's professional-experience eligibility streams (consulting, manufacturing domain expertise, IT/OT convergence, or technology consulting) prior to enrolling in the SIRI Assessor Training Course.

Skills and Attributes

The successful candidate will bring a combination of food manufacturing expertise, relationship-building skills and a proactive, market-facing mindset. They will be comfortable representing CFIN externally, building a regional network and taking ownership of measurable outcomes.
· Relationship Management:
Builds trusted, long-term relationships across the food and beverage ecosystem and establishes credibility with companies, industry stakeholders, technology providers and partners.
· Business Development Mindset:
Proactively identifies opportunities, builds a pipeline of qualified leads and connects companies with CFIN resources, programs and services relevant to their needs.
· Market Presence:
Enjoys being visible and active in the market and is comfortable representing CFIN at industry events, meetings, conferences and speaking opportunities.
· Data-Driven:
Uses data and metrics to track activity and understand outcomes. Contributes to departmental and organizational measures of success and helps document results and success stories that demonstrate CFIN’s impact.
· Manufacturing Credibility:
Brings practical, real-world experience in food manufacturing and understands the operational realities, constraints and opportunities facing processors.
· Technology & Innovation Curiosity:
Interested in how emerging technologies can address real business and operational challenges and create meaningful value for manufacturers.
· Collaboration:
Works effectively with colleagues and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds, regions and sectors. Contributes to a culture of shared learning across the national RID team.
· I ndependent & Organized:
Works effectively within established priorities and processes, manages a diverse regional portfolio, maintains strong follow-through and is comfortable working independently.
· Communication & Digital Fluency:
Communicates clearly with audiences ranging from plant-floor teams to senior executives and is proficient with CRM systems, Microsoft 365 and other digital collaboration tools. Note: ability to communicate in both of Canada’s official languages is considered an asset.
Knowledge of Canada's food innovation ecosystem, funding programs or business support organizations is considered an asset.
Ability and willingness to travel, including occasional overnight travel, as required.
Valid Drivers license in good standing and access to a reliable vehicle.
Integrity, a positive attitude and a demonstrated commitment to CFIN's mission and collaborative way of working.
To achieve a strong national membership base, CFIN must embrace diversity in all its forms, including personal, geographical and sectoral diversity; deliver services equitably in both official languages; and maintain a value proposition that resonates across the food innovation ecosystem.

Accessibility & Accommodation

Canadian Food Innovation Network (CFIN) is committed to creating an inclusive, accessible workplace that respects the dignity and independence of people with disabilities. CFIN provides equal employment opportunities and is dedicated to complying with applicable accessibility and human rights legislation across Canada.
Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment, selection and assessment process. If you require accommodation, please contact HR@cfin-rcia.ca, and we will work with you to support your participation.
We thank all applicants; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Assistant Vice President, Accounting Advisory
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

About The Job

Reporting to the Vice President and Chief Accountant, the AVP, Accounting Advisory will provide accounting advice on complex transactions, including acquisitions, divestitures, capital and tax initiatives. The role is also responsible for monitoring financial reporting trends and developments and assessing their impact on Sunlife, including regulatory change and emerging standards and topics (EST).

As a corporate function, the AVP, Accounting Advisory has global responsibilities across all of Sunlife’s business groups: Sunlife Canada, Sunlife U.S., Sunlife Asia, Asset Management and Corporate/Enterprise Services. The AVP will work as a peer to another AVP, Accounting Advisory; together, they are supported by a team of Directors and Managers.

What You'll Be Doing

Advise Business Groups and Corporate on the application of IFRS to strategic and business initiatives, M&A and other planned transactions. Collaborate with business leaders to explore alternatives, where appropriate, and develop accounting positions consistent with established policies and financial reporting requirements.
Lead the implementation of new and amended IFRS Accounting Standards and assess the impact of IASB and IFRIC developments on Sunlife’s accounting policies and disclosures.
Lead the adoption and embedding of IFRS 18, Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements, including management-defined performance measures (MPMs).
Lead cross-functional working groups to consider the implications of new requirements and develop accounting recommendations on key policy decisions.
Lead initiatives that drive continuous improvement in how we execute our work, including greater use of technology, automation and AI.
Represent accounting policy positions with the external auditors and resolve related audit enquiries.
Prepare accounting position papers and summaries of significant judgments for senior management and, where appropriate, the Audit Committee.
Develop training programs and global communications outlining new accounting policies and financial reporting developments.
Manage and prioritize multiple competing tasks and deliverables.

What You'll Need To Succeed

University degree in accounting or commerce, a CPA designation (or equivalent, such as CPA (US) or CA), and a minimum of 10 years of accounting advisory and financial reporting experience.
Experience in a public accounting firm or a large, complex public company with international operations is preferred. Prior experience in a financial institution or insurance company is highly desired; knowledge of IFRS 17, insurance products and related accounting issues is a strong asset.
Deep technical expertise, strong analytical skills and an in-depth understanding of the application of IFRS. Knowledge of US GAAP and US statutory (NAIC) requirements is an asset.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders without formal authority and to work effectively with multiple stakeholders across geographies and businesses.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical matters clearly and concisely to senior and non-technical audiences.
Ability to lead significant change across a complex, matrixed, international enterprise.
Strong people, process and project leadership skills, with the ability to mobilize internal and external resources to deliver key initiatives and projects.
Ability to develop creative yet practical solutions that meet the needs of the organization.
Experienced people leader with a solid track record of building, motivating and developing a small, high-performing team.
Logical, intellectually curious, proactive and energetic; enjoys collaborating with others while taking ownership of complex projects through to successful completion.
Thrives in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
The ambition and potential to take on more senior leadership roles in the future.

What's in it for you:

Being a member of the Sunlife family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Salary Range:

155,000/155 000 - 225,000/225 000

Job Category:

Finance

Posting End Date:

10/12/2026
